provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Living and non living things
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify living and non-living things.
The pupils should be able to list features of living things.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about things around us. Today we will learn which things are alive and which are not alive.

Content:
Living things are plants and animals that grow, eat, reproduce and die. Non-living things do not grow, eat or reproduce. Examples of living things are goat, mango tree and fish. Examples of non-living things are stone, book and chair.

Class activity:
Pupils will sort pictures of living and non-living things into two groups.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is a living thing?
2. Give two examples of non-living things.
3. How do living things grow?

Summary:
Living things grow, eat, reproduce and die while non-living things do not.

topics.title: Parts of the body
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify external body parts.
The pupils should be able to state functions of body parts.

Introduction:
We have been learning about living things. Today we will learn about the parts of our body and what they do.

Content:
Our body has many parts like head, eyes, nose, mouth, hands, legs and feet. The eyes help us see. The nose helps us smell. The mouth helps us eat and talk. Hands help us hold things. Legs and feet help us walk and run.

Class activity:
Pupils will point to different body parts as the teacher calls them out.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name two body parts on your head.
2. What do your legs help you do?
3. Which body part helps you smell?

Summary:
Our body has different parts with different functions that help us live.

topics.title: The senses
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the five senses.
The pupils should be able to identify sense organs.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about body parts. Today we will learn how we use our body parts to know things around us.

Content:
We have five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch. Our eyes help us see. Our ears help us hear. Our nose helps us smell. Our tongue helps us taste. Our skin helps us feel. These are called sense organs.

Class activity:
Pupils will visit different sense stations-one for each sense to experience different things.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name two sense organs.
2. Which sense organ helps you see?
3. What can you smell in the market?

Summary:
We use our five senses to know and understand things around us.

topics.title: Plants around us
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify parts of a plant.
The pupils should be able to state uses of plants.

Introduction:
We have learned about living things. Plants are living things around us. Today we will learn about plants.

Content:
Plants have roots, stem, leaves, flowers and fruits. Roots hold the plant in the soil and take water. Stem carries water to all parts. Leaves make food for the plant. Flowers make fruits. Fruits have seeds. We use plants for food, medicine, building houses and making furniture.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a plant and label its parts.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name two parts of a plant.
2. What do roots do?
3. How do we use plants in our homes?

Summary:
Plants have different parts and we use plants for many things in our daily life.

topics.title: Animals around us
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to differentiate between farm and wild animals.
The pupils should be able to group animals.

Introduction:
We have learned about plants. Today we will learn about animals that live around us.

Content:
Animals are living things. Farm animals are kept by people for food or work like cow, goat and chicken. Wild animals live in forests and jungles like lion, elephant and monkey. We can group animals by where they live, what they eat or how they move.

Class activity:
Pupils will sort pictures of animals into farm animals and wild animals.

Evaluation questions:
1. Give an example of a farm animal.
2. Where do wild animals live?
3. How can we group animals?

Summary:
Animals can be farm animals or wild animals and we can group them in different ways.

topics.title: Water
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list uses of water.
The pupils should be able to identify sources of water.

Introduction:
Water is important for living things. Last week we learned about animals. Today we will learn about water.

Content:
Water has many uses like drinking, cooking, washing, bathing and farming. We get water from rain, rivers, streams, wells and boreholes. We must keep water clean to stay healthy. Dirty water can make us sick.

Class activity:
Pupils will list different ways we use water at home and school.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name two uses of water.
2. Where can we get water from?
3. Why should we keep water clean?

Summary:
Water is useful for many things and we must keep it clean to stay healthy.

topics.title: Air
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify air around us.
The pupils should be able to explain moving air.

Introduction:
We have learned about water. Today we will learn about another thing around us-air.

Content:
Air is all around us but we cannot see it. We need air to live. Air helps us breathe. Moving air is called wind. We feel wind when it blows. During Harmattan season, the wind is very dry and brings dust from the Sahara.

Class activity:
Pupils will blow air to make things move like paper and feathers.

Evaluation questions:
1. What do we need air for?
2. What is moving air called?
3. How do we know air is around us?

Summary:
Air is all around us, we need it to live and we can feel it when it moves.

topics.title: Soil
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify types of soil.
The pupils should be able to state best soil for planting.

Introduction:
We have learned about water and air. Today we will learn about soil which is on the ground.

Content:
There are different types of soil: sandy soil, clay soil and loamy soil. Sandy soil has big particles and water flows through it quickly. Clay soil has small particles and holds water. Loamy soil is best for planting because it has sand, clay and organic matter. We find good soil in our farms and school garden.

Class activity:
Pupils will feel different types of soil and describe how they feel.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name two types of soil.
2. Which soil holds water best?
3. Why is loamy soil good for planting?

Summary:
Soil has different types and loamy soil is best for growing plants.

topics.title: Simple machines
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify levers around us.
The pupils should be able to explain how machines make work easy.

Introduction:
We have learned about natural things. Today we will learn about simple machines that help us do work.

Content:
Simple machines help us make work easy. A lever is a simple machine. Examples of levers are seesaw, nutcracker, shovel and broom. When we use a lever, we use less effort to move something heavy. Our arm is also a lever when we lift things.

Class activity:
Pupils will use a ruler to lift a book and see how it works like a lever.

Evaluation questions:
1. What is a simple machine?
2. Give an example of a lever.
3. How do machines help us?

Summary:
Simple machines like levers make work easier for us.

topics.title: Revision and project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what we learned this term.
The pupils should be able to present their project.

Introduction:
This is the last week of the term. We will revise what we learned and show our projects.

Content:
We learned about living and non-living things, body parts, senses, plants, animals, water, air, soil and simple machines. For our project, each pupil made a model of a simple machine. Today we will show our projects and explain how they work.

Class activity:
Pupils will present their simple machine models to the class.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name one living thing and one non-living thing.
2. What do plants need to grow?
3. How do simple machines help us?

Summary:
We have learned many things this term and we enjoyed making our projects.
